comparator.name: Bachelor Geneeskunde
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from the official 2026-2027 OER and its appendices for the Erasmusarts 2030 curriculum. The programme has a total study load of 180 EC, distributed evenly across three bachelor years. The curriculum is integrated and programmatically assessed: the OER explicitly states that separate EC cannot be assigned to individual competencies or knowledge tests. Years 1 and 2 each comprise integrated case-based medical blocks, projects and longitudinal clinical, professional, societal, academic and technology lines. Year 3 contains a 30-EC minor, 29 EC of integrated medical study and one separately identified EC for longitudinal professionalism. The component model therefore preserves the official credit-bearing structure without inventing EC for individual clinical blocks.
components: Five case-based medical blocks, projects in medical science and sustainable public health, and longitudinal clinical-skills, professional-identity, societal, academic and technology education.
Five case-based medical blocks, projects in health technology and healthcare policy and management, and the longitudinal curriculum lines.
A coherent internal or external minor completed at the start of bachelor year 3.
Advanced integrated blocks in posture and movement, brain and senses, and ageing and the final phase of life, including end products embedded in the programme.
The separately identified credit awarded for sufficient longitudinal professional conduct.

Health technology, data and responsible innovation

selection.assessment: The closest feasible UCR response covers biomedical science, body systems, disease mechanisms, health psychology, lifespan development, research, ethics and communication while preserving the absence of clinical medical training. Two further generator-backed directions remain. Population health, prevention and healthcare organisation support a policy-and-systems route; medical technology, evidence evaluation and innovation support a health-data-and-technology route. Each route is coherent, feasible and differs from every other route by at least twelve of 24 courses, so all three are included.

alternatives.label: Biomedical science, health & behaviour
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by biomedical science, human physiology, disease mechanisms, neuroscience, health psychology and research. The label states those fields without implying clinical medical education or qualification as a doctor.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response builds a non-clinical programme in biomedical science, human physiology, anatomy, disease mechanisms, pharmacology, infection, neuroscience and health psychology, supported by laboratory work, quantitative research, evidence synthesis, ethics and communication.
progression: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine and Introduction to Brain & Behavior begin the programme. Molecular Cell Biology, human physiology, biochemistry, statistics and pharmacology follow those foundations. Functional anatomy, laboratory work, abnormal psychology and perception precede the final advanced sequence in disease mechanisms, molecular pathology and genetics, higher cognition, medical and health psychology, infection and immunity, evidence synthesis and lifespan development. Every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester, and each course is marked available in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Public health, behaviour & healthcare organisations
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum concentrates epidemiology, health behaviour, lifespan health, economics, sociology, organisational leadership, public policy analysis through economics, mixed methods and public communication. The label reflects those actual fields rather than promising medical or healthcare-management credentials.
alternatives.concept: A population-health and healthcare-systems route connecting epidemiology, health behaviour and lifespan development with economics, inequality, sociology, organisational leadership, mixed-method research and ethical public communication.
alternatives.distinctness: This route removes twelve specialist biomedical, laboratory, anatomy, infection, pharmacology and cognitive-neuroscience courses from the closest match. It adds economics, econometrics, sociology, organisational leadership, diversity management and policy communication. Fourteen of the 24 courses differ in each programme, and the organising choice shifts from individual biomedical mechanisms to population outcomes, prevention and healthcare institutions.
progression: Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Epidemiology & Public Health and introductory economics establish the health and policy strands in semester 1. Research Methods & Statistics precedes every economics and leadership course that formally requires it. Introductory sociology precedes modern and contemporary social theory conceptually. Medical and Health Psychology follows the psychology gateway; advanced evidence synthesis and lifespan development follow the health and methods foundations. The final year integrates organisational leadership, econometrics, behavioural economics, diversity management and communication. Every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester, and each course is marked available in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Health data, technology & responsible innovation
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines health and biomedical foundations with programming, data science, machine learning, computer vision, databases, optimisation, AI ethics and product design. The label accurately presents a health-technology direction without claiming engineering or clinical medical training.
alternatives.concept: A health-technology route combining biomedical and health-behaviour foundations with programming, databases, data science, machine learning, medical imaging, neural networks, optimisation, AI ethics, product design and evidence synthesis.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes much of the biological sequence, cognitive neuroscience, abnormal psychology and lifespan psychology to add programming, mathematics, databases, data science, machine learning, medical imaging, neural networks, optimisation, AI ethics and product design. Twelve courses differ in each programme. It differs from the public-health route by fifteen courses, replacing economics, sociology and organisational study with computational technology and biomedical applications.
progression: The first year establishes biomedical, psychological, programming, mathematical, laboratory, AI-ethics and database foundations. Human physiology, statistics and public health precede advanced health applications. Mathematical Methods precedes Neural Networks & Deep Learning, while Introduction to Programming precedes Optimization Methods in AI. Medical imaging, evidence synthesis and health psychology lead into machine learning, product design, pharmacology and final advanced data, optimisation and disease-mechanism work. Every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester, and each course is marked available in its assigned term.

blocks: The first integrated medical year combines biomedical knowledge, clinical skills, patient contact, projects and longitudinal professional formation. No single UCR course corresponds to that complete clinical component.

The second integrated medical year combines organ-system medicine, diagnosis and treatment, clinical skills and health projects. UCR has related academic courses but no sufficiently direct counterpart to the full clinical component.
The advanced integrated medical year combines later-life and organ-system medicine with clinical and professional integration. UCR does not offer an equivalent clinical component.
Both develop professional identity, conduct and reflection; the comparator embeds medical professionalism longitudinally, while UCR offers broader personal and professional development.

The comparator reserves a 30-EC coherent minor. UCR's complete programme is elective by design, so no single scheduled UCR course is a substantive counterpart to the comparator's separate minor component.

notes.text: The Erasmus bachelor integrates biomedical science with patient contact, clinical reasoning, physical examination, treatment planning and longitudinal preparation for medical practice. UCR can combine biomedical science, health psychology, public health, policy and health technology, but it does not provide clinical medical training or a route to qualification as a doctor.
